newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks seen up on further foreign buying.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks seen up on further foreign buying.

text.p: Thai stocks are seen gaining strongly again on Friday as a backlog of unfulfilled orders and further foreign buying is expected to push the market sharply up at the opening, analysts said.
The SET Index 49.19 points, or 8.65 percent, to 617.93 on Thursday. The Index has risen 91 points since the Bank of Thailand's decision to float the baht on Wednesday.

"I expect it to open pretty strong as there is a lot of outstanding orders on the books, but I think we might see some profit taking in the afternoon, before another gain on Monday," said Philip Adkins, head of research at Nava SC.
Most stocks in the market have been up their daily 10 percent limit in early trade on the last two days, halting trade in many blue chips and reducing volumes.
Traders said many orders remain unexecuted and are likely to lift the bourse strongly at the opening.

Opening bids for frontline bank stocks were up 10 percent on Thursday's close. Investors have resorted to any stocks available in which to ride the rally though liquidity is likely to improve this afternoon as jittery investors exit ahead of the weekend, analysts said.
"I'll be very surprised if the market ends up as strongly today, but I think five to six percent is quite likely and I think we will see another rise on Monday," Adkins said.
